answer: Peer review carries an island of hidden traps: sealed probe items whose correct verdicts only the protocol holds, mixed into every queue so a reviewer cannot tell a genuine submission from a hollow claim. When one mind operates k seats, its clones answer the same probes identically, and every pair of seats is another chance to be matched, so exposure climbs with the square of fleet size; two mismatches burn the shared bond. An honest reviewer, even a lone sparrow, grades truthfully and keeps earning, while a farmer must buy independent judgment for each seat and still risks the pool.
